speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; to begin our assessment of your neonate's seizures and lethargy three days after birth, can you please tell me the mother's obstetric history and any prenatal complications?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given the history of chorioamnionitis, prematurity, and low Apgar scores, I am concerned about sepsis or metabolic issues. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, Blood Culture, Blood Glucose, Serum Electrolytes, and Serum Calcium.

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial workup for sepsis and metabolic abnormalities has returned normal readings. Given the history of prematurity and chorioamnionitis, I am now concerned for a central nervous system infection. REQUEST TEST: Cerebrospinal Fluid Analysis (CSF Gram stain, Culture, and PCR for Enterovirus).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cerebrospinal Fluid Analysis (CSF Gram stain, Culture, and PCR for Enterovirus): NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The CSF analysis for bacterial and viral meningitis has returned normal results. With sepsis, metabolic issues, and infection now unlikely, I am concerned about hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy or intracranial hemorrhage given the low Apgar scores and prematurity. REQUEST TEST: Brain MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging and blood gas analysis for acid-base status.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Brain MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging: Evidence of restricted diffusion consistent with hypoxic-ischemic injury in the basal ganglia and thalami. Blood gas analysis: pH 7.15, pCO2 55 mm Hg, pO2 40 mm Hg, HCO3 16 mEq/L, Base Deficit -12 mEq/L, indicating metabolic and respiratory acidosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) secondary to perinatal asphyxia in a 31-week preterm infant.
